content: @Devon Tuma can you give me the lowdown on the interaction between the new dependent OracleSpec and IsPerIndexQueryBound? It looks like OracleSpec ι is now defined so that each input to the oracle can have it's own type, and iota is no longer an index into different oracles, but different oracle inputs I guess? I am trying to bound the number of queries the merkle tree protocol makes to the hash function usingIsPerIndexQueryBound but lets you specify the number of queries per index, which seems like it lets me limit how many times I call the hash function on a particular input, but not the number of hash function calls overall. Is there a different way I'm supposed to talk about this bound?

You need IsQueryBound for counting more than just the specific input value, I think IsPerIndexQueryBound is maybe a misleading name now that input+index are bundled. But something like this:

def IsHashBound {α ι τ : Type} {hash_spec : OracleSpec ι} {spec : OracleSpec τ}
    (oa : OracleComp (unifSpec + hash_spec + spec) α) (n : ℕ) :=
  IsQueryBound oa n (fun _ _ => True) (fun | .inl (.inr _) => n - 1 | _ => n)

is probably what you want. There should maybe be a full API for this "decrement on a specific predicate and accept everything in canQuery" case

Besides the fact the above is wrong (the 'can query' pred isn't actually guarding anything and needs to be stronger), it can also be replaced entirely with IsQueryBoundP oa n (. matches ...) now, to avoid manually doing the accounting

In Verified-zkEVM/VCV-io#365 I have bashed through with enough AI compute to prove the extractability theorem with OracleComp.IsTotalQueryBound, but the next step is probably to generalize it and make it compatible with defining the BCS transform, so I can probably make an IsQueryBoundP version too. Is it easier for you if I do these in separate PRs or all at once?
I'd probably suggest just getting it merged now if only so other PRs don't screw up your changes with merge conflicts or anything but I don't have strong preferences personally
